page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated single x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor core operating at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 1 vCPU and 1 execution thread. The CPU core features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, with architectural support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local ephemeral NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core processing capabilities derived from the high base clock and Zen 4 architecture. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 3029.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1946.0, placing it within the top 25 percent of tested systems. However, overall throughput is strictly constrained by the single-thread configuration, as seen in an identical multi-core stress-ng metric and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1938.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 26.49 GB/s on large-block writes and 33.86 GB/s on large-block reads, with small cached read transfers measuring 147.38 GB/s.

Because the r7a.medium combines an 8.0 GB memory footprint with a single compute core, it offers resource efficiency for applications that require substantial memory per thread rather than parallel compute capacity. With no bundled local disks, persistence is fully dependent on remote block storage volumes. The configuration is suitable for low-throughput in-memory caching layers, Redis instances with moderate working sets, background batch workers, and development or staging environments for memory-bound services.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a single-core, memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 vCPU (1 physical core, 1 thread) accompanied by 8.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, resulting in an 8:1 RAM-to-core allocation. The CPU architecture supports AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, along with hardware-assisted cryptographic operations. Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread performance, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 1946.0, though aggregate capacity is bounded by the single execution thread. The instance contains zero local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network storage for persistence. The r7a.medium is well-tailored for small in-memory datastores, lightweight caching tiers, single-threaded backend tasks, and memory-oriented development environments.
